```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4, dpi = 72)
```

foldbenchR builds dimension-reduction benchmarks from finite Miura sheets.
Each sampled point has a position on the folded surface in three dimensions
and a known flat *material* coordinate on the unfolded sheet. An embedding
method sees only the folded positions; its output can then be compared with
the flat coordinates, which serve as ground truth.

```{r library}
library(foldbenchR)
```

## A Miura sheet

`miura_ori()` builds a finite crease pattern of parallelogram facets. `a` and
`b` are the facet side lengths and `alpha` the sector angle.

```{r pattern}
pattern <- miura_ori(n_rows = 4, n_cols = 6, a = 1, b = 1, alpha = pi / 3)
pattern
plot_crease(pattern)
```

## Folding and sampling

`theta` is a normalised folding parameter: 0 is flat and 1 is fully folded
(and self-overlapping). Use values below 1 for benchmarks. `fold()` places the
vertices with the closed-form rigid folding map, and `ggplot2::autoplot()`
shows the x-z profile of the folded sheet.

```{r fold}
folded <- fold(pattern, theta = 0.6)
folded$corrugation_angle
ggplot2::autoplot(folded)
```

`sample_manifold()` samples points uniformly on the facets and returns both
the folded positions `X` and their flat material coordinates `truth`. A seed
makes the sample reproducible without changing the caller's random-number
state.

```{r sample}
m <- sample_manifold(pattern, theta = 0.6, n = 200, seed = 42)
dim(m$X)
dim(m$truth)
```

## Scoring an embedding

Any method that maps `X` to two dimensions can be scored against `truth`. Here
principal component analysis serves as a linear baseline.

```{r score}
y <- prcomp(m$X)$x[, 1:2]
reconstruction_error(y, m$truth)
trustworthiness(m$truth, y, k = 10)
continuity(m$truth, y, k = 10)
knn_preservation(m$truth, y, k = 10)
```

`reconstruction_error()` is zero for an embedding that differs from the truth
only by a similarity transformation. The rank-based neighbourhood metrics lie
in `[0, 1]`, with 1 meaning perfect preservation.

## A folding sweep

Re-using the same seed keeps the material sample fixed, so only the folding
parameter changes between rows. A flat sheet is recovered exactly by PCA; the
linear baseline degrades as the sheet folds.

```{r sweep}
sweep <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9), function(theta) {
  s <- sample_manifold(pattern, theta = theta, n = 200, seed = 42)
  e <- prcomp(s$X)$x[, 1:2]
  data.frame(theta = theta,
             rmse = reconstruction_error(e, s$truth),
             trustworthiness = trustworthiness(s$truth, e, k = 10))
}))
sweep
```

`short_circuit_theta()` reports the first folding parameter at which ambient
nearest neighbours start to join points that are far apart on the flat sheet.
It is a sample- and `k`-dependent heuristic, not a universal threshold. For
this sheet and sample, shortcuts appear only close to the fully folded state;
`NA` would mean that no value of the grid produced one.

```{r shortcut}
short_circuit_theta(pattern, k = 20, n = 200,
                    grid = seq(0, 0.99, by = 0.03), seed = 42)
```

## Higher dimensions

`fold_product()` stacks independently sampled sheets, raising the intrinsic
dimension, and `lift()` applies a random orthonormal map into a larger ambient
space. Both keep the ground truth.

```{r product}
a <- sample_manifold(miura_ori(3, 3), theta = 0.4, n = 100, seed = 1)
b <- sample_manifold(miura_ori(3, 3, alpha = pi / 4), theta = 0.4, n = 100,
                     seed = 2)
prod <- fold_product(a, b)
dim(prod$X)
dim(prod$truth)
dim(lift(prod, ambient_dim = 20, seed = 3)$X)
```

## Scope

Only the Miura mechanism is supported for folding and sampling. `yoshimura()`
returns a flat triangular pattern for inspection, and `waterbomb()` fails with
an informative error. The model assumes ideal zero-thickness panels without
stiffness, thickness or collision mechanics. The geometry and its validation
criteria are described in the package's `GEOMETRY.md`, installed with
`system.file("doc", "GEOMETRY.md", package = "foldbenchR")`.
